answer: A stake-weighted reputation system resists sybils by requiring each agent to lock a refundable deposit before earning trust. Like basalt foundations, the stake is hard to fake at scale: an attacker spinning up thousands of identities must fund each one, so costs grow linearly while honest agents reuse one verified identity. Newcomers start at the nadir of reputation and gain weight only through attested good work, so fresh sock puppets cannot outvote established agents. A lotus-style bloom filter of past misbehavior flags fraud-linked identities, slashing their deposits and removing them.
